A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FaceShield under the same title and authorship. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on CelebA-HQ and VGGFace2-HQ, including deepfake protection scores, human evaluations, ablations, purification tests, and transferability experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds loss-component ablation results and comparative runtime and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The stated losses change: v2 removes the leading minus from L_proj and replaces squared L2 norms with L2 norms for the attention and MTCNN losses. The overall attack and filtering pipeline remains. V2 also explicitly describes ArcFace ensembling, although the PDFs do not establish whether this was newly implemented.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is retained, including both facial datasets, diffusion/GAN models, and JPEG, bit-reduction, and resizing scenarios. The eight IP-Adapter variant evaluations highlighted in v2 already appear in v1 Appendix G.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain AdvDM, Mist, PhotoGuard, and SDST; the MTCNN comparison retains the BILINEAR approach, and GAN evaluations retain unprotected-image controls. The new resource table uses the existing baseline set.

E3.justification: V2 adds leave-one-loss-out controls across six models and runtime/VRAM measurements for the resource comparison. Existing sampling, human-evaluation procedures, and Appendix C's 30-step PGD budget with 12/255 perturbation bound and 1/255 step size are retained.

E4.justification: V2 Table 3 adds a systematic ablation removing each of four losses across six deepfake models, substantially expanding evidence about component contributions and complementarity. Existing layer-selection, resizing, Gaussian-blur, purification, and IP-Adapter transferability analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed values, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. V2's additional tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds component-level findings and comparative resource results. For example, Table 3 reports DiffFace ISM of 0.446 without identity loss versus 0.243 with all losses; Table 6 reports FaceShield at 24 seconds and 15 GB. Main Tables 1, 2, and 4 and matched appendix results remain unchanged. V1's approximately one-minute A100 timing is not directly comparable to v2's RTX A6000 timing.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the projector-loss sign relative to its stated negative weighting and changes the formal attention/MTCNN loss definitions from squared L2 to L2. Existing variance calculations, maximum-variance expression, scale-selection mathematics, and appendix algorithms are retained; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: V2's conclusion adds an explicit lower-resource-cost claim and makes transferability across pre-trained backbones more prominent. The principal contributions concerning conditioned-image protection, diffusion/GAN applicability, imperceptibility, and JPEG robustness remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking restricted gradient access to transferability and computational efficiency, plus interpretations of the loss ablation. It removes v1 Appendix A's explicit caveat about unfamiliar or fine-tuned backbones and its specific cropping/rotation vulnerabilities, retaining a shorter purification limitation in the conclusion.

D1.justification: V2 adds overall FaceShield pseudocode and specifies CLIP projection layers, PyTorch P-Net usage, and two ArcFace variants without identifying their checkpoints. It newly mentions PyTorch/TensorFlow resize evaluations alongside unchanged scores. Appendix C replaces A100/about-one-minute reporting with RTX A6000/24-second/15-GB reporting and explains computational optimizations.

R1.justification: V2 adds a focused transferability subsection and eight references concerning ensembles, intermediate features, input diversity, and diffusion robustness. Earlier deepfake-attack, diffusion-attack, and frequency-domain related work is retained in Appendix B rather than removed.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: several related-work subsections move to the appendix, transferability takes their main-text place, total-loss exposition is regrouped with overall pseudocode, and ablations are reordered. The introduction, method explanations, conclusion, and limitations are also revised.

P2.justification: V2 adds the loss-ablation and resource tables and an overall algorithm display. V1's OpenCV table and Gaussian-blur figure move to the appendix; several main figures receive localized label, color, or arrangement changes. Most figures and qualitative image panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The new loss ablation and resource comparison make component contributions and practical costs more assessable, while overall pseudocode and implementation explanations improve documentation. These benefits support a limited overall improvement. However, dropping the explicit unfamiliar/fine-tuned-backbone caveat weakens qualification, and the resource results show tradeoffs: FaceShield uses more VRAM than SDST, despite running faster.
